title: Provenance
description: Where a record came from and how much of it was observed rather than concluded. Every normalized Archie record carries one of these; it is the single most important object in the world-intelligence model. A globe with dots on it is a toy. A globe where every dot can be traced back to the byte a provider returned, through each transformation that touched it, is an instrument. This block is what makes the second thing possible, which is why nothing may omit it.

source.description: The immediate upstream this record came from.

upstream.description: Sources behind the immediate one, nearest first. An aggregator that republishes a national agency's feed lists the agency here, so a reader can tell a primary source from a repeater.

fetched_at.description: When Archie retrieved it. Distinct from when the event happened and from when the provider published it, because the three routinely differ by hours and the gap is itself a signal.

published_at.description: When the provider published it, where the provider says so.

observed_at.description: When the underlying phenomenon actually occurred, where it is known.

kind.description: raw: as the provider returned it, only reshaped. inferred: Archie concluded it. curated: a human or a maintained dataset asserted it. verified: independently reproduced or cross-source corroborated. A record may only claim `verified` if `corroboration` names at least two independent sources.

confidence_band.description: A band, never a fabricated percentage. A single number invites arithmetic that the underlying evidence does not support; a band forces the reader to look at `corroboration` for the actual basis.

corroboration.description: Independent sources that assert substantially the same thing. Independence is the point: three outlets republishing one wire story is one source, not three, and the pipeline is required to collapse them before recording corroboration.

agreement.description: A contradicting source is recorded, never discarded. Disagreement between sources is information.

raw_reference.description: How to get back to exactly what the provider returned. Without this, a derived record cannot be audited and a mistake cannot be traced to its origin.

record_id.description: The provider's own identifier, kept verbatim so an update can be matched to the record it supersedes.

transformations.description: Ordered list of what Archie did to the raw payload. A reader should be able to reconstruct the path from provider bytes to this record.

implementation.description: Module and version that performed the step, so a bad transformation can be attributed and rolled back.

model.description: Set when a language model performed this step. Its presence means the output is model-derived and must not be treated as observation.

license.description: What Archie is permitted to do with this record. Carried per record rather than per provider because a single provider often mixes terms across its endpoints.

access_class.description: restricted means the record may be used internally but never rendered to a shared display or exported.

freshness.description: How current this is expected to be. A layer whose data has outlived its cadence must visibly dim rather than continue to look authoritative.

provider_id.description: Matches a provider manifest id, e.g. `usgs.earthquakes`.
